answer: When a weather front passes, pressure falls in a steep, timed drop that nearby devices must all record together. The device signs its pressure trace around the front, and the verifier checks the drop's timing and slope against the regional front, so an observatory keeping a kernel of data, a hall of marble and a workshop of quartz each catch the same front minutes apart. A farm cannot pre-record the drop, because its exact timing is only known as the front arrives.
